architecture_reasoning.pattern_identified: Governance system with user proxies, epoch-based voting, and multiple initiative types (BribeInitiative, CurveV2GaugeRewards, UniV4MerklRewards). Users stake LQTY through their proxy, allocate votes to initiatives, and initiatives receive BOLD rewards based on vote share. The system has time-based epochs and requires UserProxy deployment for staking.

instance_counts.description: Deploy minimal viable system in setup(), use helper functions for additional instances

choices.audit_reason: @audit Single governance instance required - it's the central coordinator, deploying multiple makes no sense

config_variations: different governance addresses would break system
choices.audit_reason: @audit Deploy 1 in setup for basic testing, add helper_deployBribeInitiative() to test multiple initiatives with different bribe tokens. Each initiative can have a different bribe token which creates meaningful state space exploration.
@audit NOT deploying in setup - this is optional and can be deployed via helper. Uses helper_deployCurveV2GaugeRewards() to test different gauge configurations.
@audit NOT deploying in setup - this is optional and can be deployed via helper. Uses helper_deployUniV4MerklRewards() to test different Uniswap V4 pool configurations.

scenarios_covered: Basic governance staking and vote allocation
BOLD reward distribution based on votes
scenarios_NOT_covered: @audit NOT TESTING: Multiple governance instances - makes no architectural sense
@audit NOT TESTING: CurveV2GaugeRewards and UniV4MerklRewards in initial setup - these are optional reward mechanisms that can be tested via helpers
@audit NOT TESTING: Complex multi-user delegation patterns beyond 2 actors - keeping complexity manageable
@audit NOT TESTING: Migration from V1 staking rewards (ETH gains) - MockStakingV1 provides basic functionality but complex V1 migration scenarios are out of scope
architecture_reasoning.trade_off_summary: Chose moderate complexity by deploying 1 BribeInitiative in setup with helper functions to deploy more. This allows basic testing immediately while giving fuzzer control over when/how many additional initiatives are deployed. Skipped deploying CurveV2GaugeRewards and UniV4MerklRewards in setup since they're optional reward mechanisms - fuzzer can deploy them via helpers if needed.

dynamic_deployments.name: bribeInitiatives
dynamic_deployments.reason: Fuzzer should be able to deploy multiple BribeInitiatives with different bribe tokens to test competition, different token decimals, and multi-initiative scenarios. Registration is manual via governance.registerInitiative().

dynamic_deployments.name: curveV2GaugeRewards
dynamic_deployments.reason: Optional reward mechanism - fuzzer controls if/when to deploy. Allows testing gauge integration scenarios without cluttering initial setup.

dynamic_deployments.name: uniV4MerklRewards
dynamic_deployments.reason: Optional Merkl rewards integration - fuzzer controls deployment. Allows testing different pool configurations and weight distributions.

custom_mocks_needed.name: stakingV1
custom_mocks_needed.reason: Requires specific ILQTYStaking interface implementation with stake/unstake and reward tracking. Standard MockERC20 cannot fulfill this role.

custom_mocks_needed.name: liquidityGauge
custom_mocks_needed.reason: Required for CurveV2GaugeRewards testing - needs deposit_reward_token functionality. Used only when deploying CurveV2GaugeRewards via helper.

custom_mocks_needed.name: distributionCreator
custom_mocks_needed.reason: Required for UniV4MerklRewards testing - needs Merkl-specific campaign creation interface. Used only when deploying UniV4MerklRewards via helper.

tokens.name: lqty
tokens.reason: LQTY is the governance/staking token. Needs MockERC20Tester for permit functionality (EIP-2612). Not using AssetManager because LQTY has a fixed role and is not swappable.

tokens.name: lusd
tokens.reason: LUSD is received as rewards from V1 staking. Used by MockStakingV1 and UserProxy. Fixed role, not swappable.

tokens.name: bold
tokens.reason: BOLD is the primary reward token distributed to initiatives based on votes. Also used for registration fees. Fixed role in governance, not swappable.

tokens.name: bribeToken
tokens.reason: Token used for bribes in BribeInitiative. Each BribeInitiative can have a different bribe token. Using MockERC20Tester for standard ERC20 functionality.

time_sensitive.reason: System is heavily epoch-based. Governance uses block.timestamp for epoch calculations, voting cutoffs, and reward accrual. Need vm.warp() to test epoch transitions, voting windows, and time-locked features like initiative registration/unregistration.

multi_user.reason: Need 1 additional actor (total 2) for testing different users staking, voting, and claiming. System has permit functionality (depositLQTYViaPermit) which requires valid signatures, so needs_private_key is true to use the hardcoded actor with known private key for permit testing.

proxy_deployment.reason: Users must interact through UserProxy contracts for staking LQTY in V1. The UserProxy is created via governance.deriveUserProxyAddress() and deployed via governance.deployUserProxy() (or auto-deployed on first stake). Required for all staking operations.

struct_params.reason: Used by depositLQTYViaPermit(). Rather than having fuzzer generate complex permit signatures, we generate valid permits via _getValidPermitParams() helper. Single mode is sufficient - one valid permit is all we need.
Used by BribeInitiative.claimBribes(). Contains epoch and prevAllocationEpoch values. Single instance simplifies fuzzing - fuzzer can still call with arrays containing this single struct.
Passed to initiative hooks like onAfterAllocateLQTY(). Read from governance.userStates() so we don't need fuzzer to generate it. Single cached instance for admin testing.
Passed to initiative hooks like onAfterAllocateLQTY(). Read from governance.lqtyAllocatedByUserToInitiative() so fuzzer doesn't generate it. Single cached instance for admin testing.
Passed to initiative hooks like onAfterAllocateLQTY(). Read from governance.initiativeStates() so fuzzer doesn't generate it. Single cached instance for admin testing.

helper_functions_needed.name: _getDeployedBribeInitiative
helper_functions_needed.reason: Get a deployed BribeInitiative by index from deployedBribeInitiatives array. Modulo wrapping for fuzzer convenience.

helper_functions_needed.name: _getDeployedCurveV2GaugeRewards
helper_functions_needed.reason: Get a deployed CurveV2GaugeRewards by index. Only needed if fuzzer deploys via helper.

helper_functions_needed.name: _getDeployedUniV4MerklRewards
helper_functions_needed.reason: Get a deployed UniV4MerklRewards by index. Only needed if fuzzer deploys via helper.

helper_functions_needed.name: _getCurrentEpoch
helper_functions_needed.reason: Get current epoch from governance contract. Useful for fuzzer to know current state.

helper_functions_needed.name: _getValidPermitParams
helper_functions_needed.reason: Generate valid EIP-2612 permit signatures using the known private key. Required for testing depositLQTYViaPermit() without fuzzer having to generate valid signatures.

audit_notes: @audit chose moderate setup because the system has clear core contracts (Governance, 1 BribeInitiative) that must exist, but benefits from fuzzer-controlled deployment of additional initiatives
@audit NOT TESTING: Multiple Governance instances - architecturally nonsensical, Governance is a singleton coordinator
@audit NOT TESTING: CurveV2GaugeRewards and UniV4MerklRewards in initial setup - these are optional reward distribution mechanisms that can be deployed via helpers if fuzzer explores those paths
@audit NOT TESTING: Complex V1 staking migration scenarios with ETH gains - MockStakingV1 provides basic stake/unstake but complex V1 migration is out of scope
@audit NOT TESTING: More than 2 actors - system supports arbitrary users but 2 actors (address(this) + 1 additional) is sufficient to test multi-user interactions while keeping state space manageable
@audit ASSUMPTION: Using START_TIME and EPOCH_DURATION constants from existing setup - these match the deployment test values
@audit ASSUMPTION: BribeInitiative deployed in setup uses a generic bribeToken - fuzzer can deploy additional BribeInitiatives with different tokens via helper

@audit ASSUMPTION: All struct parameters use single mode because they're either generated by helpers (_getValidPermitParams) or read from governance state - fuzzer doesn't need to generate these complex structs
@audit UNCERTAINTY: Whether to track ETH rewards from V1 staking - MockStakingV1 supports it but adds complexity. Keeping it for completeness.
@audit chose to NOT deploy UserProxy in setup because governance auto-deploys it on first stake via _increaseUserVoteTrackers(). Storing the address after first deployment for convenience.
@audit chose needs_private_key=true because depositLQTYViaPermit requires valid EIP-2612 signatures. Using hardcoded actor 0x537C8f3d3E18dF5517a58B3fB9D9143697996802 with known private key.
@audit Trade-off: Deploying only 1 BribeInitiative in setup vs 0 - chose 1 because most tests will use BribeInitiative and it's the primary initiative type. Helpers allow deploying more.
@audit Trade-off: Using MockERC20Tester vs standard MockERC20 - chose MockERC20Tester because it has permit() functionality needed for depositLQTYViaPermit testing
@audit Coverage gap: Not testing initiative hook gas limits (MIN_GAS_TO_HOOK) - this is a security feature but difficult to test in fuzzing without custom malicious initiatives
@audit Coverage gap: Not testing registration/unregistration edge cases around UNREGISTRATION_AFTER_EPOCHS - these require precise epoch timing that may be hard for fuzzer to hit

@audit Design choice: Storing struct parameters in Setup rather than having fuzzer generate them - this simplifies fuzzing since these structs are either derived from contract state or require complex signature generation
